Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The two commands (`makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`) will only: (1) download the .deb source from `download-mem.nowledge.co` (the package's own upstream domain, consistent with the `url` field `mem.nowledge.co`), (2) extract it to allow auditing, and (3) source the PKGBUILD top-level scope. The top-level scope contains only plain variable assignments with no command substitution, backticks, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or any other dangerous operations. The `source_x86_64` entry uses `${pkgver}` which is a safe shell variable expansion, not command substitution. There is no `pkgver()` function defined, so nothing runs there. No `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions execute because `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` stop before those stages. The checksum is present (not SKIP). No malicious behavior occurs during these specific commands.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code executes during the narrow gate commands.</summary>
</security_assessment>
